races.name: CopyBet Daily World Cup Profit Boost Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Manowest
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in good form (P3 last two in-running), well-handled by Sean Bowen, and suited by this good ground based on strong similar-going record; his ability to set a comfortable tempo without a rival forcing him gives him a significant race-shape advantage, though the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.93 is a mild flag.

runners_data.name: Captain Boudet
runners_data.note: Veteran of good-ground chases with a habit of finishing second (two recent runner-up efforts), though his hold-up style requires a strong pace that is not guaranteed with only Manowest setting the tempo; Rian Corcoran claims 5lbs which softens the burden, but his trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/8 is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Mix Of Clover
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old who is remarkably consistent on good ground (15 similar-going runs, 3W 8P), well placed by jockey Tom Broughton (3lb claim) to travel prominently and capitalise on Manowest's controlled lead; his recent 3-3 form suggests he remains competitive, though his age and a trainer with no winners from five recent runs warrants a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Aslukgoes
runners_data.note: Fundamentally a front-running type whose natural role is at or near the head of affairs, but with Manowest already owning that position and Mix Of Clover and White Riot pressing, James Bowen will struggle to slot him into a prominent berth; a run of out-of-the-places finishes (4-U last two) reinforces the concern, and the STYLE_FIT discount is warranted here.

runners_data.name: White Riot
runners_data.note: A six-year-old trained by the in-form Fergal O'Brien who has bumped into trouble over 2m in the past and now steps up to 2m4f — a trip that may unlock extra stamina; Kielan Woods should find a prominent position straightforwardly and his one win in seven similar-going appearances came at this sort of trip, making him an interesting runner to watch through the race.

runners_data.name: Evening Tess
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this lightly-raced four-year-old whose recent form (1-2-2 last three) is strong and who carries the lightest weight in the field at 156lbs; she will race from a hold-up position and needs the pace to be sustained, but her class edge and the Skelton yard firing at 8/23 in 14 days make her the primary hold-up threat if the tempo holds up.

runners_data.name: Boskill Borden
runners_data.note: Returning from 281 days off for a small Irish yard with one runner in 14 days and a lowly OR of 79 — those flags alone demand caution; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, his last few runs on good ground show minor placing form from the rear, but the layoff and lack of prep work make it very hard to assess how sharp he arrives.

races.paceDynamic: Manowest is the confirmed lone front-runner in a seven-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, he can dictate a controlled, honest gallop across the 2m4f on good ground at Worcester. Mix Of Clover and White Riot will press prominently behind him, creating a structured, single-file shape from an early stage rather than a messy scramble. Evening Tess and Captain Boudet will settle in the hold-up berths, needing the pace to be sustained enough to produce a meaningful test in the closing stages. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind the leader and pick up in the final quarter-mile — a sustainable front-running tempo rewards those with class and jumping fluency rather than pure finishing speed. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate: Aslukgoes and Boskill Borden are natural front-running or prominent runners shuffled rearward by congestion, and it is Manowest, Mix Of Clover, and White Riot who are most likely to actually secure their positions at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Test
scenarios.trigger: If Manowest dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the field strings out behind him from the third fence.
scenarios.body: Manowest controls every yard of the race, with Mix Of Clover and White Riot tracking him at a respectful distance; the test becomes who has the most left in the tank jumping the last two fences. Prominent travellers with clean jumping records are favoured as the pace is genuine but not brutal, rewarding staying power over raw acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough through the middle section to expose front-runners, allowing hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Evening Tess, lightly burdened at 156lbs and trained by the in-form Dan Skelton, times a late run off a genuinely fast tempo and cuts down the leader between the last two fences. Captain Boudet could also benefit if his rider Rian Corcoran produces a well-timed challenge, though his inconsistent form on good ground is a concern.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Manowest is never pressed and the gallop eases mid-race, allowing him to sprint clear from the front at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: A false pace suits a horse already in front — Manowest extends his advantage at the second-last and runs his rivals into the ground before they can mount a meaningful challenge. His recent Worcester form and good-ground comfort (8 runs on similar going, 1W 5P) make this a plausible alternative.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners push forward unexpectedly, creating a scrambling early pace that causes jumping errors and fallers.
scenarios.body: Crowded conditions at fences cause errors and bring hold-up horses into contention far sooner than intended, with the race thrown wide open inside the final mile. Boskill Borden — a true hold-up type who has been placed over this trip on good ground — could theoretically profit, though long absence (281 days) and a lowly OR of 79 cap expectations sharply.

watchPoints.text: Manowest's jumping — if Sean Bowen gets a clean round up front, the entire race shape depends on him not making an error that lets Mix Of Clover or White Riot barge through; any mistake at a fence could hand prominence to a rival and destabilise the predicted controlled pace.

Watch where Aslukgoes settles in the early stages — James Bowen may try to push forward toward his natural prominent role and if he succeeds he will press Manowest, converting this from a controlled single-paced race into a more contested gallop that would dramatically benefit hold-up horses Evening Tess and Captain Boudet.

Evening Tess's jumping at pace merits monitoring — she is young (four years old), lightly experienced in chasing, and if she makes errors under Harry Skelton she may not be able to land the hold-up challenge her style demands at this trip.

Boskill Borden should be observed in the paddock and early in the race given 281 days off — any sign of ring-rustiness or jumping errors would confirm he is not a factor, while surprising freshness would make him marginally more interesting as a late threat at big odds.

Mix Of Clover's stamina for 2m4f is proven (multiple wins and placings over this sort of trip on good ground) but he is 12 years old — watch whether he still travels with his customary fluency after jumping the 13th or 14th fence, as any sign of laboured jumping would signal he is feeling the distance.

races.name: Amodil Group Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Doyouknowwhatimean
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and race shaper, with 2 wins from 5 runs on Good going in similar form history at this trip; at 9 years old and 168lbs he is not at his lightest, but the uncontested lead flatters his chance and Gary Hanmer's stable is in decent form at 2/10 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Getaway Vic
runners_data.note: Beautifully placed for this race shape — six runs on Good going have produced 2 wins and 5 places and his recent back-to-back second placings over 2m2f-2m3f suggest he has the fitness and profile to be on the premises at the death when tracking a single front-runner.

runners_data.name: Betty's Tiara
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's mare has tumbled down the weights but her last two runs at 2m3f on Good came back ninth and seventh, which is a concern; headgear (tongue-tie/blinkers noted in profile) may sharpen her, but her Good-going strike rate of 1W from 15 runs is a live flag.

runners_data.name: Always Busy
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose instinct will be to push forward, but with several others ahead of him in the pecking order for that position, Jack Tudor is likely to find himself settled further back than ideal — his 34-day absence and a fall in recent form (F, 6) add to the uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Ridin Solo
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's eight-year-old has finished second and third on his last two starts and is sharp enough by inclination to want prominent ground, but this field cannot accommodate him there; his Good-going record is only 3 places from 12 runs without a win on that surface, which tempers expectation if he ends up in midfield.

runners_data.name: Grillon De Monty
runners_data.note: At 11 years old he is the oldest in the field, yet his recent course-relevant form (2/22f/Good and 1/23f/Good) is very live and he has a 2W5P record on Good across 15 runs — the natural front-runner in him will want to race prominently and if he gets near his preferred position he becomes interesting despite the redistribution note.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: The one genuine hold-up horse in the field, and Nick Scholfield's stable is 0/13 over 14 days which is a context flag; however his form reads 1/26f/Good, 3/26f/Good and he is proven at big distances on this surface, so if the pace quickens mid-race he has the staying profile to pick up pieces late.

races.paceDynamic: Doyouknowwhatimean is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to press from the outset, he should be able to bowl along at a measured, self-selected gallop over this 2m7f trip on Good ground at Worcester. Behind him, Getaway Vic and Betty's Tiara are the most natural secondary prominent types who should slot in directly behind, while Always Busy, Ridin Solo, and Grillon De Monty are all genuine front-to-prominent racers by inclination but cannot all occupy that territory — they are mapped to midfield because the race shape physically cannot accommodate them. Of those three, Grillon De Monty's course-and-distance form and Ridin Solo's recent Hereford runner-up effort suggest they are the most motivated to push forward, with Always Busy most likely to be squeezed back further than ideal. With a single, unfussed pace-setter controlling a small field at a sustainable tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can travel within striking range and quicken from two out, rather than true hold-up operators who need a searching gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Doyouknowwhatimean Leads, Close Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Doyouknowwhatimean sets a controlled, uncontested gallop and the race is won by a horse who travels prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Doyouknowwhatimean dictates from the front at a fair but unhurried clip, and the winner is found among those tracking closely in second or third, pouncing from the second-last fence as the pace sharpens. Getaway Vic and Betty's Tiara are ideally placed to benefit, with both having the prominent profile and course-relevant Good-ground form to deliver a challenge at the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so uncontested and modest that Doyouknowwhatimean simply slips the field from the final turn and none of the tracking horses can respond.
scenarios.body: With the pace entirely in Doyouknowwhatimean's hands and no horse exerting pressure, he conserves energy through the back and finds enough reserves to kick clear from three out before the field can organise a challenge. His Good-ground form at this trip is solid and Gary Hanmer's runners have returned 2 wins from 10 in the 14-day window, keeping him live in this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Get Involved Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and allow the horses mapped to midfield to close ground from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early tempo — perhaps if Grillon De Monty or Ridin Solo push forward to their natural position and increase the pace — would string the field out and create an opportunity for Edgewell to stay on powerfully from off the pace. Edgewell's hold-up profile, Good-ground record of 3W7P, and recent winning run at 2m4f makes him the primary candidate to capitalise, though the pace scenario required is genuinely dependent on the redistributed horses not settling quietly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Prominent Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed horses push forward to contest the early gallop, creating a more competitive pace that scrambles the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: Ridin Solo, Grillon De Monty, and Always Busy all attempting to secure prominent ground would create a ragged, pressured tempo, increasing the risk of jumping errors or tactical confusion and making the race harder to predict from the front. In this chaotic shape, a horse like Getaway Vic who can sit just off a contested pace and switch off efficiently becomes even more dangerous, as does the well-handicapped Edgewell stalking the mess from behind.

watchPoints.text: Grillon De Monty and Ridin Solo — if either or both push forward to their natural position early, the expected controlled gallop fractures and the entire race shape changes, increasing pace and altering who benefits.
Edgewell's stable (Nick Scholfield) is 0/13 in the 14-day trainer window — a cold yard flag worth tracking in betting markets before accepting him as a confident each-way proposition.

Always Busy — a 34-day absence combined with a recent fall and a form string of P23-F6 over different trips means his jumping reliability on a return after a month off is the key risk for those backing him.

Betty's Tiara — watch her early in the race; if she fails to travel fluently in the first mile and struggles to hold prominent ground, her chance evaporates given her recent record at this distance on Good ground.

Doyouknowwhatimean's jumping under pressure — as the lone front-runner he controls his own rhythm early, but if challenged at any fence from the home turn his record of unseated/pulled-up runs in recent form (P, P) warrants monitoring for any jumping hesitation.

races.name: Amodil Group Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Kiwi De Cotte
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with course form (1W at 23f good ground), Dan Skelton's excellent 14-day strike rate, and a P-style that naturally maps to the front here — confirmed sole pace-setter and the most straightforwardly placed horse in the race.

runners_data.name: Yellow Card
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over for Mickey Bowen and this four-year-old has a winning hurdle run over 22f on good ground — though his natural style is hold-up, the field congestion means he likely ends up further back than ideal and must produce a strong late run.

runners_data.name: Annual Invitation
runners_data.note: Christian Williams runner who has shown nothing in five recent starts, none over this trip — a genuine hold-up type who will sit towards the rear rather than feature prominently, and the form figures (3279-5) offer little encouragement on good ground at 2m4f.

runners_data.name: Geordie Mackem
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison sends this flat-bred recruit (all Flat form on the AW) over to jumps after a massive 489-day absence — entirely unproven over hurdles and over this trip and distance, with 0/19 for the trainer over 14 days; the layoff alone makes him a very difficult proposition to assess.

runners_data.name: Regarde
runners_data.note: The most logical horse to press Kiwi De Cotte given a P-style and multiple placed efforts over 2m5f-2m8f on good ground; the tongue-tie is in place, he ran 12 days ago in a return that brings him forward, and Gavin Sheehan is an informed booking at Worcester.

runners_data.name: Saint Arion
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. rides a horse with a poor recent sequence (P0-46) and no wins from three hurdle starts — by nature a hold-up operator, he will find himself in the middle of the pack and needs a significant step up from his latest efforts to feature.

runners_data.name: Solo Eclipse
runners_data.note: Trainer David Killahena & Graeme McPherson are in good form (5/8 T14) and a tongue-tie is fitted, but five hurdle starts have produced no win and the horse consistently finishes in mid-division — a true rear-of-field type who will need the front to collapse to be involved.

runners_data.name: Tufton
runners_data.note: 249 days off the track and just three hurdle runs to his name, carrying a tongue-tie; Philip Rowley's runner is an unknown quantity returning from a long absence, and while good-ground form exists over 20f, the ring-rustiness at this level is a serious question mark.

runners_data.name: Virtuose D'ainay
runners_data.note: Thomas Gallagher's seven-year-old carries a clear form warning — flagged as fading in finishes — and a string of poor efforts (3/PP9-) suggest the horse lacks the class or jumping consistency for this field; 78 days off does not obviously remedy those issues.

races.paceDynamic: Kiwi De Cotte is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Harry Skelton's six-year-old should dictate alone from the front over this 2m4f on good ground at Worcester — a track where uncontested leaders can be particularly hard to reel in. Regarde is the only other natural prominent type and will likely slot in behind, creating a small front group with the remainder strung out in a pack behind. The pace will be honest but sustainable, set by a single horse with no reason to over-cook it, which means the race is likely to develop into a test of jumping fluency and staying power rather than a tactical sprint. This shape overwhelmingly favours Kiwi De Cotte and any horse able to travel economically in second or third, with true hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage. Multiple runners — Saint Arion, Geordie Mackem, Annual Invitation, Yellow Card and Solo Eclipse — are genuine hold-up types pushed into the midfield representation on the map; of these, Regarde is the runner most likely to actually press forward and secure a prominent position naturally.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kiwi Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kiwi De Cotte leads without pressure and sets a measured, sustainable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Kiwi De Cotte controls the tempo from the front, conserves energy over the obstacles, and kicks clear turning for home on ground that suits; no rival has the tactical speed to overhaul a horse that has never been headed on this type of trip. Harry Skelton's positive handling and Dan Skelton's strong recent form rate (13/27) add further confidence that the front-running plan is executed properly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Regarde Tracks And Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Kiwi De Cotte makes a jumping error or weakens after the second-last and Regarde, travelling prominently, pounces.
scenarios.body: Regarde has the course form at this distance on good ground (two placed efforts at 2m5f and 2m8f), travels prominently as a natural P-style runner, and Gavin Sheehan will have him perfectly placed to capitalise on any chink. The tongue-tie is familiar headgear and the 12-day turnaround on a fit horse at Worcester suits Snowden's operation.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kiwi De Cotte burns off too fast on the flat Worcester track and stops abruptly in the straight, releasing held-up horses into the finish.
scenarios.body: A genuine meltdown at the front would open the race up for the better-class hold-up horses — Yellow Card (Sean Bowen, good-ground winner at this trip) and Annual Invitation are the most credentialed of the rear-guard. However, this scenario is tempered because so many of these closers are racing out of their natural rear role having been redistributed, and true come-from-behind finishing speed in this field is limited.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Staying Contest
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is pedestrian, bunching occurs mid-race and a staying grind over the final two flights sorts them out.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run race can scramble the field and bring stamina-heavy, unexposed types into play — Tufton and Solo Eclipse, both with turf headgear and limited miles on the clock over hurdles, might outstay rivals who have exposed their ceilings. This is the least likely shape given the probable presence of at least one organised front-runner, and neither of these horses has form figures to inspire confidence.

watchPoints.text: Kiwi De Cotte's jumping is the pivotal factor — if Harry Skelton lets him bowl along cleanly at the front, this field may struggle to land a blow, but any stumble at a hurdle hands momentum straight to Regarde.

Yellow Card is being ridden by Sean Bowen who will want to ride positively, but the horse's genuine hold-up profile means a tussle between natural instinct and jockey intent — watch for him to be steered wider than ideal if the early pace bunches the field.

Geordie Mackem returns from nearly 500 days off the track with entirely flat-race form — an early mistake or signs of ring-rustiness could cause interference in a field of nine, particularly in the early hurdles.

Tufton's 249-day absence and limited hurdle experience (three runs) means his jumping may be untested at pace — monitor his jumping at the first two obstacles to assess whether he settles into the race or becomes a traffic hazard.

Annual Invitation's last five efforts show a horse that simply cannot get competitive at this grade; Jack Tudor will have to produce a completely transformed performance, and backers of hold-up scenario winners should note this horse is not the banker of that group despite an OR of 120.

races.name: Amodil Group Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: American Mike
runners_data.note: Proven at this course and distance (wins at Worcester 2m4f Good), arrives 29 days fresh for Olly Murphy who is firing at 4/13 over 14 days; a genuine hold-up specialist who needs the pace to be honest enough to set up his late run, and Tom Hutsby claims 10lb.

runners_data.name: Skyjack Hijack
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here, though Sean Quinlan's mount has historically raced more prominently than as a pure leader — a STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in how comfortable it is dictating solo; five wins from 14 on Good ground suggests the conditions suit, and 55 days off is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Miss Maverick
runners_data.note: Won 12 days ago and is back quickly for Gary Hanmer (1/7 over 14 days), which is a very thin recent trainer strike rate worth noting; has 2m4f course form on Good and prefers to race prominently, a position she should be able to claim with her experience.

runners_data.name: Our Guide
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in his last three hurdle starts and an exceptional 4/4 win record in similar going, making him the standout form pick in this field; Jamie Snowden's yard is active (4/10 over 14 days), Gavin Sheehan is a shrewd jockey in races like this, and the step up from 2m2f to 2m4f looks likely to suit this improving five-year-old.

runners_data.name: Ebony Warrior
runners_data.note: Won over 2m3f on Good ground last time and showed ability when fresh, but his natural prominence is compromised here — he is one of three prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred position, and the resulting midfield berth may blunt his effectiveness; Nick Slatter's 3lb claim is a partial compensation.

runners_data.name: Dream Diamond
runners_data.note: Has a history of jumping issues (unseated, pulled-up) that demand respect in a hurdles context, and his Good-ground record across 11 runs shows only one win; Jonathan Burke picks up the ride for the in-form James Owen (9/46 over 14 days), though the horse's front-running instincts will be tested in a crowded prominent group.

runners_data.name: Billy Boi Blue
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who wants to race prominently but sits in a field already overcrowded with similar types — he is the lowest-rated runner here (OR 112) and his recent form of 5-6 does not suggest he can overcome the positional disadvantage; Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim partially offsets the weight, but the tactical squeeze is a real concern.

races.paceDynamic: Skyjack Hijack is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good ground at Worcester over 2m4f, is likely to establish a controlled, honest gallop from the outset without serious pressure — this is a genuinely uncontested lead. Behind him, Our Guide, Miss Maverick, and the redistributed trio of Ebony Warrior, Dream Diamond, and Billy Boi Blue all want to race prominently, meaning there is far more pace-pressure in the chasing pack than the map can accommodate, and several of those horses will be squeezed into a midfield they do not naturally occupy. American Mike is the only true hold-up runner, sitting last or near-last as the field sorts itself out through the early stages. This shape — a lone leader setting a sustainable tempo with a congested, slightly frustrated prominent group behind — classically favours a horse who can track the pace from second or third without burning energy fighting for position, then quicken from the front of the chasing group; Our Guide, who has been winning readily on Good ground, fits that profile most cleanly, and genuine hold-up finishers like American Mike also have a route into the race if the pace is real enough to string the field out. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their position — Ebony Warrior, Dream Diamond, and Billy Boi Blue are most likely to lose ground to Our Guide and Miss Maverick, who carry the form and jockey quality to assert their natural spots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Skyjack Leads, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Skyjack Hijack sets a controlled solo lead and one or two prominent types track him cleanly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Skyjack Hijack dictates a fair but unhurried tempo, leaving the race to develop into a two-furlong test of stamina and jumping accuracy from the top two in the market; horses who secure a prominent position early without burning fuel in scrimmaging are perfectly placed to collar him. Our Guide's relentless Good-ground form and clean jumping make him the prime tracker-to-winner, while Miss Maverick has the course form to grab second.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Lifts, Stayer Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group pushes the tempo higher than Skyjack Hijack would choose, genuinely stringing the field out.
scenarios.body: A stronger early gallop suits the lone hold-up runner American Mike, who has winning form at this course and distance on identical going and arrives fresh off a 29-day break for the in-form Olly Murphy yard; he would be delivered with a single run from the back with Tom Hutsby claiming. The energy cost on the prominent scramblers would blunt their finishing kicks, leaving the true stayer room to reel them in up the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling among the redistributed horses causes a brief surge and then a settling that leaves Skyjack Hijack and one prominent rival in clear air.
scenarios.body: Skyjack Hijack benefits if the cavalry charge behind him burns itself out, and he gets a soft lead that converts to an unassailable advantage at the last; Miss Maverick, fresh from a recent win and with course form, is best placed of the chasing group to avoid the chaos and sit clean. The runners mapped out of their natural style — Ebony Warrior, Dream Diamond, Billy Boi Blue — pay the highest price in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp a Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Skyjack Hijack crawls and no other horse forces the tempo, setting up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A very slow pace theoretically suits hold-up horses arriving late, but American Mike is the only genuine hold-up type and the prominent runners would simply coast and quicken — making this scenario largely a prominence race in disguise. Dream Diamond's Good-ground speed gives him an outside shout in a flat-out dash, though his form figures on Good ground are modest and this outcome depends heavily on a sequence of events that require multiple horses to race against their instincts.

watchPoints.text: Our Guide's jumping must be monitored — five consecutive wins have come partly on the back of clean rounds, and any hesitation at a hurdle on this 2m4f course could cost him the prominent pitch he needs.

Watch the early break from Ebony Warrior, Dream Diamond, and Billy Boi Blue — if all three attempt to push up to their natural position behind Skyjack Hijack, a brief surge in pace could scramble the shape of the entire race in the first mile.

Skyjack Hijack has not run for 55 days and is stepping into an unaccustomed lone-leader role; if fitness or confidence wavers jumping, the controlled tempo that underpins the dominant scenario collapses.

American Mike carries 168lbs — the heaviest burden in the race — and while he is proven at this level, that weight combined with a hold-up style means his late run must be perfectly timed by Tom Hutsby to bridge the gap.

Miss Maverick is on a quick turnaround (12 days) for a trainer with a 1/7 recent strike rate — if she shows any signs of a flat performance early, the prominent spot she needs may be surrendered to Our Guide, which would narrow the competitive field significantly.

races.name: Martin Keighley Racing Club Handicap Hurdle Race (Div I)

runners_data.name: Sun Joy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win over 21f on Good going 72 days ago and solid recent form including a second over this trip; carries top weight but has the class to justify it, and racing out of a pure prominent tag into the lead role slightly overcooks his style_fit reading — he is the one to beat.|

runners_data.name: Idaho Fire
runners_data.note: James Owen runner returning from 66 days off with only one comparable run on Good ground; his form figures on Soft dominate the record and the drying conditions here are a query, making this largely an unknown quantity on current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Little Ledgend
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen booking is significant, and Olly Murphy's runner has been placed in five consecutive starts including a second on Good ground most recently; consistent but yet to win in ten Good-ground runs, and the tongue-tie headgear is a retained aid.|

runners_data.name: Play Pretend
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with an excellent record on Good going — two wins and seven places from fourteen attempts — so the surface suits well; his latest run was a modest third at a lower level, but the style and ground profile align strongly with today's conditions.|

runners_data.name: The Secret Pearl
runners_data.note: Alex Hales runner with a tongue-tie, operating as a natural hold-up type who has placed twice from seven Good-ground starts; 21 days since last run is no concern, but the back-of-field style may not be rewarded if Sun Joy nurses the pace.|

runners_data.name: Estacas
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran trained by Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole who has placed twice on identical Good going in his recent past; a hold-up horse wearing a hood, he has the ground profile but his form figures show a cluster of 8s on Good and he is competing off a 97 OR, which is not his most comfortable territory.|

runners_data.name: Bells Of Ufford
runners_data.note: Tim Vaughan runner wearing tongue-tie and hood, who was placed most recently after a string of moderate finishes; a natural hold-up horse and the most recent run was encouraging, but his Good-ground record is modest and he is off a career-low OR of 92.|

runners_data.name: Mancero
runners_data.note: David Pipe's four-year-old holds the lightest weight in the field and Jack Tudor is a significant jockey booking; his win came on Good going over 20f and the style profile — prominent to midfield — puts him in the race, though a pulled-up run last time and a hood are flags to monitor.|

runners_data.name: North Account
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's six-year-old has not won or placed in four Good-ground starts and carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish tag; genuinely a back-of-field hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield because the rear is congested — his true style will leave him without the late pace injection this shape needs.|

runners_data.name: Strong As Steel
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll runner without a win or place on Good ground in four attempts, and a natural hold-up horse whose position in the map is a function of field compression rather than genuine tactical flexibility; the headgear note (b) and modest OR of 78 make this the most exposed runner in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Sun Joy is the clear front-runner here, and with no confirmed challenger willing to press him from the off, he should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground over 2m4f at Worcester. Little Ledgend, Play Pretend, and Mancero will compete for prominent positions just behind him, meaning the race will have a steady-to-fair early pace that compresses the field rather than stringing it out. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear — North Account and Strong As Steel are true closers who have been mapped to midfield because Estacas, The Secret Pearl, and Bells Of Ufford occupy the natural back-of-field positions, so North Account and Strong As Steel are unlikely to get the late cover they need. With a single uncontested leader setting a manageable tempo and a cluster of prominent-to-midfield types tracking close, this race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can race prominently, travel smoothly, and kick from the front or just off it — hold-up horses face a significant disadvantage if the pace is not truly searching.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sun Joy Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sun Joy dictates an uncontested lead and the field settles without challenge.
scenarios.body: Sun Joy sets his own terms from the front, the pace stays honest but not brutal, and he retains enough reserves to extend at the second-last hurdle; this is exactly the shape his best form — including his win over similar conditions — suggests he is built for. Prominent horses tracking close throughout are ideally placed and the most likely to mop up any late weakness.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Sun Joy ties up in the closing stages and one of the tracking prominent horses produces a decisive late surge.
scenarios.body: The contested midrace pace from Little Ledgend, Play Pretend, and Mancero means one of them finds themselves in the perfect position when Sun Joy's effort flattens out approaching the last; Sean Bowen on Little Ledgend and Jack Tudor on Mancero carry the strongest jockey profiles to capitalise on this exact shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected early and creates a truly strong gallop that burns off the leaders.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-anticipated tempo would suit horses tracking just off the pace and finishing stoutly, with The Secret Pearl — a consistent hold-up performer on Good ground — capable of picking off weakening rivals; Estacas has two placed efforts on identical going and represents the alternative finisher if the race develops this way.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Land It
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses the field completely and a genuine late run from the rear becomes viable.
scenarios.body: North Account and Strong As Steel are natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield due to field composition, making their ability to find clear daylight in a compressed finish genuinely uncertain; this scenario requires everything to go wrong for the prominent horses and is the least likely shape given the race's controlled pace profile.

watchPoints.text: Sun Joy and Little Ledgend — if these two finish first and second it will confirm the pace map exactly; watch whether Little Ledgend's jockey Sean Bowen settles immediately behind Sun Joy or challenges for the lead, as any early pressure fundamentally changes the race shape.

Mancero — Jack Tudor on a lightly-weighted four-year-old trained by David Pipe is a combination that often wins races it should not; watch the market for any significant move, as unexposed horses with this profile can land gambles.

North Account — tagged as fading in the finish and redistributed from true hold-up to midfield on the map; if he is allowed to drift back to his natural position at the rear, he is highly unlikely to land a blow and backers should understand the map position is not his genuine tactical ground.

The Secret Pearl — Kielan Woods tends to be aggressive with hold-up types at Worcester; if he pushes forward early rather than dropping in, the horse is racing out of role and the late-finishing profile becomes irrelevant.

Idaho Fire — Jonathan Burke's 66-day absence and uncertain form on Good ground makes this runner a volatile unknown in betting terms; an opening show significantly shorter than expected would warrant attention given the stable's pattern with returning horses.

races.name: Martin Keighley Racing Club Handicap Hurdle (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Scintillante
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with strong going-identical credentials (14 runs, 2 wins, 7 places on good), Jonathan Burke booking is positive, and returning after just 23 days; will need to be in the right position at the business end of what looks a steadily-run race.

runners_data.name: Lacrima
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact trip on good ground at Worcester 9 days ago, which is the most relevant form line in the race; Jack Stenhouse's 7lb claim helps, though the quick turnaround and tongue-tie merit monitoring in a field where pace will be slow.

runners_data.name: Faded Fantasy
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor is a strong jockey booking for Christian Williams, but this mare has finished eighth in both her good-ground starts over 2m4f this season and the trainer is 0/9 in the last 14 days; her hold-up style suits the shape but recent form figures are hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Present Fair
runners_data.note: Donald McCain runner returning from 308 days off and carries a tongue-tie; her natural style is hold-up but she has been redistributed to midfield in this map — she is a true closer who may struggle to secure a comfortable position in a field stacked with similar types.

runners_data.name: Bashful Boy
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 10-year-old is 225 days off the track (with a fitness flag) and races in a hood; a genuine rear-of-field operator whose redistribution into midfield reflects how congested the hold-up ranks are, making it hard to see him landing a blow fresh on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Boston Savr
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes and has zero wins or places from five starts on good or soft going; placed in midfield on the map despite being a natural closer, and with a tendency to weaken late, Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will need things to fall perfectly — which they may not in a race this stacked behind the pace.

runners_data.name: County Champs
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the pivotal pace-setter; his form shows consistent placed efforts up front (three second places on good ground), and returning from 211 days off is the primary risk — if fit, he controls this race from flag to finish.

runners_data.name: Harry Gulliver
runners_data.note: Absent for 589 days, which is the longest layoff in the field and a significant concern; won over 2m on good ground in his form peak and is a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield by map redistribution, meaning his early position may be less tractable than ideal on return.

runners_data.name: Could Be You
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes and has a grim recent record (two pulled-ups, a ninth, and two falls or pulled-ups in five runs); Bradley Harris's 3lb claim is a minor aid, but this is a horse finding life very difficult at present and the midfield redistribution compounds an already difficult profile.

runners_data.name: Illico De Montave
runners_data.note: Rosemary Gasson runner returning from 313 days off wearing a hood for the first time; has never finished in the first six across 11 runs and, while mapped into midfield, is a natural rear-of-field horse — the combination of layoff, headgear debut, and limited form makes this a very difficult win case.

races.paceDynamic: County Champs is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control tempo from the front at a sustainable, measured gallop on good ground over 2m4f. With nine horses broadly classified as hold-up types — many of them genuine off-the-pace operators — the field will string out behind County Champs in a procession, creating a steady-run race that puts a premium on finishing speed rather than stamina grinding. Present Fair, Bashful Boy, Boston Savr, Harry Gulliver, Could Be You, and Illico De Montave are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield because there are far more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the back; County Champs is virtually certain to secure the lead, and Scintillante, Lacrima, or Faded Fantasy are most likely to genuinely travel prominently behind. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours a horse with a potent late kick who can travel smoothly just off the steady pace and produce a decisive run from two out, rewarding the best-quality closer over this trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: County Champs Leads, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If County Champs controls a steady gallop and the field queues up behind, allowing a well-positioned closer to pounce from two out.
scenarios.body: County Champs sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo that compresses the field mid-race and leaves the race wide open for a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace; the final two hurdles become the decisive zone where finishing quality wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sufficiently slow that a wall of closers arrives simultaneously at the last, turning it into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop compresses the field until the home turn, where multiple horses make their move simultaneously and the outcome hinges entirely on raw acceleration; horses with strong recent form figures at this trip on good ground hold the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: County Champs Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If County Champs is permitted to dictate such a moderate gallop that its rivals fail to quicken past after a flat, undemanding race.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to press County Champs into a genuine test, it could conserve enough energy to repel challengers in the straight, making the prominent position pay on good ground at this course.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Injected Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses is forced to race more positively than planned, injecting a genuine mid-race surge that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected middle mile would expose stamina limitations in lower-rated closers and elevate horses who handle a true gallop on good ground, with durable types rewarded at the expense of one-paced hold-up specialists.

watchPoints.text: County Champs sets the entire tempo — watch whether Freddie Gordon allows it to bowl along at a true gallop or barely trots, as that single decision determines whether this is a sprint finish or an endurance test.

Lacrima's fitness after just 9 days since her last run is the key variable for what looked an impressive recent win; any sign of laboured jumping or flat travelling should be noted early as evidence the quick return has found her out.

Harry Gulliver and Present Fair are both returning from layoffs of 589 and 308 days respectively — if either shows signs of greenness or hesitancy at the early hurdles it will confirm they need the run and should be discounted immediately.

Boston Savr and Could Be You are both flagged for fading in finishes and are true hold-up horses racing in a congested rear group; watch how far back they settle at halfway, as any horse tracking them for a lead run could find the well dry by the time they reach the second-last.

races.name: Amodil Group Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Best Night
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid Good-ground form (1W6P on similar going), has placed at this trip twice in five runs; Rian Corcoran (5lb claim) partners for David Pipe, who is 1/8 over 14 days — an in-form yard with a live runner tracking the pace.

runners_data.name: Mistral Milly
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy takes the ride for D J Jeffreys and this hold-up mare has been off 58 days; her best going form is on Good (4/16f/GOO) but she has zero wins or places on similar ground across 11 runs — stamina reserves are her best asset if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Lucy The Wire
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, and while her OR of 100 tops the field, note the STYLE_FIT flag — she is stepping up from a hold-up role and her recent form has been inconsistent (8th last time); Sean Bowen's track record makes her hard to dismiss up front, but she is racing in a position that does not reflect her recent patterns.

runners_data.name: Caterpillar Girl
runners_data.note: Tom George runner carrying hg:t (tongue tie) and returning 23 days after a pulled-up run; her form string shows falls and a P in recent starts, making her jumping reliability a genuine concern, though her two best efforts on Good ground at 2m show she handles conditions if she gets round.

runners_data.name: No Risk Today
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's runner has a consistent record of running without winning (0W0P on similar going across five runs) and drops to OR 88 — a true hold-up horse who, in this race, will find himself closer to midfield than he prefers, which works against his natural finishing pattern.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: The most experienced horse in the field (age 9) with a strong similar-going record (2W6P from 15 runs) and a placed effort last time out (3rd); Lee Edwards rides for a small yard (T14: 0/1) but course-and-distance familiarity is a real asset here, and she races prominently which suits this shape.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Annie
runners_data.note: Claire Hitch's seven-year-old has managed just a pull-up and a fourth in recent starts; naturally a hold-up horse but this race forces her into midfield — her Going stats are acceptable but the style displacement means she will not be racing to her strengths today.

runners_data.name: Charlotte Square
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding saddles this lightly-weighted four-year-old returning after 380 days off — that layoff is the dominant concern here; her hurdles form over Good ground has produced nothing notable (0W0P from 12 runs), and as a hold-up type now displaced into midfield, the conditions and absence stack against her.

races.paceDynamic: Lucy The Wire is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good ground at Worcester over 2m, she is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish — Sean Bowen will likely dictate terms and keep this race honest without it turning into a sprint-fest. Best Night and Quick Of The Night are the natural prominent horses who will want to track close to the pace, and with only one genuine leader, both should get comfortable positions just off Lucy The Wire without a fight for position at the head of affairs. The field does, however, hold more hold-up horses than can realistically settle at the back — No Risk Today, Jukebox Annie, and Charlotte Square are all true hold-up types who will be forced to race closer to midfield than is natural for them, meaning the back of the field may not be as congested as it appears. This controlled, single-pace gallop over a sharp 2m trip strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort — the prominent and close-tracking profile is best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lucy The Wire dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the race is run at an even tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Lucy The Wire sets a sustainable pace and the horses tracking her — Best Night and Quick Of The Night — get a perfect lead to turn into a straightforward gallop to the line; neither is asked to make a sudden gear change that favours hold-up horses. Good ground suits prompt movers here and the prominent profile is rewarded with a clean run from the final bend.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and Lucy The Wire sets a tempo that burns off the close trackers.
scenarios.body: Should the gallop be faster than expected — perhaps pressured by Best Night pushing up — the race could open up late for horses coming from further back; Mistral Milly and Caterpillar Girl, who race off the pace, are the most naturally credentialed to benefit. The hold-up types mapped to midfield (No Risk Today, Jukebox Annie) are not true closers in this race shape, which limits the depth of the late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates All
scenarios.trigger: If Lucy The Wire is allowed a completely uncontested, slow early pace and none of the prominent horses close the gap until too late.
scenarios.body: A slow-run affair turns into a sprint finish from the front — Lucy The Wire, having conserved energy, kicks clear before the final flight and holds on; her Good-ground form confirms she is capable of sustaining an effort when not pushed. Best Night, racing prominently, is the main threat if she can match Lucy The Wire's quicken, but the front runner controls the race from the saddle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If the race is disrupted by jumping errors, fallers, or horses racing in uncharacteristically forward positions causing interference.
scenarios.body: Charlotte Square (380 days off, unknown jumping profile) or Caterpillar Girl (F in recent form) could cause disruption, scrambling the order and creating a messy race that suits a horse able to adapt; Quick Of The Night's experience over course and distance (2W6P on similar going) could see her pick her way through trouble. The winner in this shape is likely whoever avoids trouble rather than whoever has the best tactical position.

watchPoints.text: Charlotte Square has been off 380 days and her jumping record over hurdles is unproven at this level — monitor her in the parade ring and early in the race for any signs of ring-rustiness or hesitancy at flights that could cause interference.

Caterpillar Girl's recent form includes a fall (F) and a pulled-up run — her jumping reliability is a live concern in an 8-runner field where one blunder could directly impact horses tracking close to her.

Lucy The Wire is tagged STYLE_FIT with a 0.92 discount — if she does not lead confidently from the gate, the entire race shape changes; watch her at the start and in the early stages to confirm she actually takes up her expected front-running role.

No Risk Today, Jukebox Annie, and Charlotte Square are all genuine hold-up horses racing out of their natural position — if they crowd the midfield together, there is a risk of traffic issues on the bend, which could affect Best Night and Quick Of The Night tracking through.

Good ground throughout the card at Worcester has been consistent all evening — no false rails or ground changes are expected to alter pace dynamics, confirming the pre-race pace map is reliable for this final 2m contest.

races.name: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hold Your Fort
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with strong good-ground form (12 runs on similar going, 3W7P) and solid recent form including a win at 2m4f; stretching to 2m7f here but the form suggests stamina is not an issue at age 10, and the amateur 7lb claim from Mr J P Murray slightly offsets the 168lb burden.

runners_data.name: Oneinthewell
runners_data.note: Five-year-old on a quick turnaround (5 days) which always warrants monitoring for freshness, has done most of his recent work on soft so the step back to good is an unknown — 4 runs on similar going produced just 1W2P — but his recent second at 2m on good is encouraging for this step up in trip; natural hold-up type that will need a proper gallop to deliver his finish.

runners_data.name: Spitalfield
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr takes the ride for the O'Neill yard who are 2/18 in the last 14 days; recorded back-to-back placings on good ground at 2m6f and 2m5f in his latest outings and the trip step-up here to 2m7f looks ideal for a horse who stays strongly — 37-day absence is not alarming given the encouraging recent form.

runners_data.name: Jefe Triunfo
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon's seven-year-old has a troubled recent record (U807 in his last three) and wears a visor; his true style is hold-up but with so many closers in this field he is likely to race further forward than comfortable, which dilutes his chance — good-ground form is solid across 13 of 14 runs but the erratic form figures give little confidence.

runners_data.name: Iamcelestialgift
runners_data.note: McPherson yard in strong form (7/10 in 14 days) and a tongue-tie is fitted; a genuine hold-up horse whose best recent form at Worcester (6th on good, 2m4f) leaves questions about the extra distance, and with the rear of the field congested he will race in midfield rather than his preferred position — the 31-day break is manageable.

runners_data.name: Stiletto
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a top booking for Sophie Leech's eight-year-old who runs in a hood and has reasonable good-ground figures (9 runs, 2W2P) but his last four runs have all been mid-to-rear finishes; naturally a hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the field dynamics, and the 33-day break coming into a long-trip race on good ground means fitness is probably fine but his closing kick off a slow pace is his main chance.

runners_data.name: Mexican Stan
runners_data.note: Carries a tongue-tie and has shown genuine aptitude for good ground (6 runs, 1W1P) with a recent win at 2m5f on good suggesting the trip is within range; a natural hold-up horse who will be forced to race closer than he prefers given the crowded rear — his last run fifth on good at 2m4f keeps him in the picture here for Alastair Ralph, but T14 figure of 0/8 is a concern.

runners_data.name: Ballela Blaze
runners_data.note: Thomas Gallagher's eight-year-old returns after 60 days but has excellent course-form profiles on good ground — three seconds and a third in recent runs — and the longer trip suits a horse whose form consistently shows him running on late; a genuine hold-up type that will be running in midfield rather than his natural position, which is a mild inconvenience, but his ability to stay and finish is the real asset here.

runners_data.name: Pooroldmackley
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter and a 7lb claimer (Miss Eleanor Williams) taking the ride for the in-house Williams yard; last run was a fourth at 2m on good and he has been placed twice in 8 runs on similar ground, but the marked jump in trip to 2m7f is a genuine stamina query — if she gets tired in the final mile the race blows open.

runners_data.name: Fane Court
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy partners this eight-year-old returning after 27 days with no wins on good or heavy ground across six runs (0W0P on similar going) which is a significant flag; has tended to finish fourth in modest company and the trip at Worcester on evening good ground does not obviously suit — a true hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by the field composition, and the form figures suggest limited upside.

runners_data.name: Alderley Charlie
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse who fades in the finish, which is a serious concern over 2m7f; the six-year-old wears a tongue-piece and hood, returns after 51 days, and his only comparable form on similar going (2 runs, 0W0P) produced a second at 2m4f on soft last time — the finishing-line warning combined with the lack of good-ground wins makes him difficult to support despite modest hurdling experience.

races.paceDynamic: Pooroldmackley is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no credible challenger for the lead, she will dictate a controlled, honest gallop over 2m7f on good ground at Worcester — a track that rewards horses who can travel comfortably and pick up late rather than those who need to be delivered in a sprint. The pace is likely to be genuine but not brutal, set by a lightly-weighted amateur-ridden mare who has previous form at the trip, meaning the race will be run at a tempo that keeps the field honest without blowing them apart early. The vast majority of this field are genuine hold-up horses — Stiletto, Jefe Triunfo, Iamcelestialgift, Mexican Stan, Ballela Blaze, Fane Court and Alderley Charlie are all natural closers and cannot all occupy their preferred position simultaneously, meaning several will race closer than ideal simply by virtue of the field dynamic. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses with good jumping, the stamina to see out 2m7f on good ground, and the ability to travel prominently or make headway from midfield turning in — true hold-up tactics off a single moderate front-runner over this trip historically leave horses with too much to do.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pooroldmackley Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Pooroldmackley sets an uncontested, metronomic gallop and the field settles in a long strung-out line behind her.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard, the closers expend energy chasing rather than tracking, and those who have tracked her in second or third are best placed to pounce at the last hurdle; the trip and good ground reward stamina and positional sense over raw finishing speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Field
scenarios.trigger: If Pooroldmackley's pace is slightly stronger than expected and the prominent trackers weaken, leaving a gap for the best-quality hold-up horses to thread through.
scenarios.body: The early leaders pay for a fraction too much pace in the middle section and the race fragments in the straight, allowing the strongest stayers to reel them in; good ground suits horses with a high cruising speed who can maintain rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Dawdle
scenarios.trigger: If Pooroldmackley sets an unusually slow tempo and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint-finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A slow pace compresses the field and makes positional advantage from the last flight decisive; horses that jump well and can quicken off a flat pace benefit most here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Stamps Out Field
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors and the 2m7f trip on a draining evening card takes a heavy toll, reducing the competitive field significantly in the latter stages.
scenarios.body: Late fallers or tired horses open the door for the most resolute stayer who has jumped cleanly throughout; low draw on fitness and freshness become decisive factors in a race of errors.

watchPoints.text: Pooroldmackley — monitor whether she is setting a true or falsely slow gallop; if she is allowed to crawl, the field will bunch and her lead evaporates, dramatically changing who benefits in the straight.

Hold Your Fort and Ballela Blaze — both have strong place profiles but neither has a recent win; if the gallop is honest these two represent the most likely finishers but punters should watch for any jumping mistakes given the 10-year and 8-year ages respectively.

Oneinthewell — a 5-day turnaround for Jonathan Burke's mount is the shortest recovery in the field; watch in the parade ring for any signs of sweat or unsettled behaviour that could signal the quick return has taken a toll before the race even starts.

Iamcelestialgift and Mexican Stan — both carry tongue-ties and both are being trained by yards in active form (McPherson 7/10, Ralph 0/8); the contrast in yard momentum means Iamcelestialgift is the one to watch if the hold-up shape delivers, while Ralph's cold run tempers Mexican Stan's claims despite the progressive profile.

Alderley Charlie — the "fades in finish" tag is critical over 2m7f on an evening card that has already seen six races on good ground; watch how he travels in the back straight, and if he is visibly off the bridle before the final turn his chance is effectively gone.
